issues.title: Internal class missing sealed keyword
issues.description: Internal implementation classes that are not designed for inheritance must be marked with the 'sealed' keyword. The WebSocketWrapper class is an internal implementation class that should be sealed to prevent unintended subclassing.
issues.rule_name: Sealed Keyword Required for Internal Implementation Classes

issues.title: Incorrect boolean operator in regex validation
issues.description: The test assertion uses AND (&&) operator instead of OR (||) when checking if the log message matches either the old or new CSP error pattern. This causes the test to fail because a log message cannot simultaneously match both regex patterns - they represent different browser error message formats. The original intent was to accept either format, but the AND operator requires both patterns to match at the same time, which is impossible. This will cause the test to fail even when receiving a valid CSP error message in either format.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
Assert.True(
    ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(logs[0].Message) &&
    ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(logs[0].Message),
    $"Expected log message to match one of the CSP error patterns: {ParseErrorMessageRegexOld} or {ParseErrorMessageRegexNew}. Actual: {logs[0].Message}");

issues.title: Disposal order causing potential race condition
issues.description: The connection disposal order is reversed - disposing secondConnection before the connection that is still being used. In the test, 'connection' performs an InvokeAsync call and its TaskCompletionSource (tcs) is awaited immediately before disposal. However, disposing secondConnection first may cause premature cleanup of shared resources or message handlers since both connections share the same user ('*'). This can lead to flaky test behavior where the connection's pending operations are interrupted by the disposal of secondConnection, especially in distributed scenarios where both connections interact with the same Redis backplane.

issues.title: Race condition from premature TaskCompletionSource recreation
issues.description: The _receiveTcs TaskCompletionSource is recreated before checking if the buffer is zero-sized, creating a race condition in the WebSocketWrapper's ReceiveAsync implementation. When a zero-byte read occurs (buffer.Count == 0), the method returns early with the result but the TCS has already been reset. This means if another thread or the background task tries to set a result on the now-recreated TCS while this zero-byte read is in progress, it will affect the next receive operation rather than completing the current one. This breaks the synchronization contract and can cause message loss or out-of-order receives in the stateful reconnection test scenarios where WebSocket message sequencing is critical.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The modified test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate phases, violating the required AAA comment pattern.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64685 - [release/9.0] Update dependencies from dotnet/arcade

structured_output.summary:
This PR is a Maestro dependency-flow update that moves the dotnet/arcade dependencies from `9.0.0-beta.25562.4` to `9.0.0-beta.25626.6` (commit `ab5773ac`) in `global.json`, `eng/Version.Details.xml`, and `eng/Versions.props`, together with the associated `eng/common` pipeline and PowerShell helper changes. The version pins are internally consistent and the tooling changes are sensible hardening (`-UseBasicParsing`, null-safe `LocateVisualStudio`, updated internal feed URL and source-build image).

The diff also carries test changes unrelated to the dependency bump, and two of them are wrong. The Components E2E CSP assertion now uses `&&` between two mutually exclusive regexes, so `EmbeddingServerAppInsideIframe_WithCompressionEnabled_Fails` can never pass. The SignalR Redis `WebSocketWrapper` moves its `_receiveTcs` reset above the zero-byte early return, which drops the frame that the SignalR client's 0-byte-then-buffered read sequence depends on. Both should be fixed before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The dependency pins themselves are correct, but the diff introduces a deterministic test failure (AND of two disjoint regexes that can never both match one log entry) and a message-losing ordering change in the Redis WebSocket test double used by the stateful-reconnect test. These need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
This repository builds through the Arcade SDK, pinned in `global.json` (`msbuild-sdks`), `eng/Version.Details.xml`, and `eng/Versions.props`. Maestro dependency-flow updates those pins and also syncs the shared `eng/common` build/pipeline scripts that CI consumes. `.azure/pipelines/ci.yml` includes the Arcade templates for source build and source indexing, so a version bump reaches both the MSBuild SDK used to build the repo and the YAML/PowerShell helpers used on build agents.

This PR moves the Arcade dependency from `9.0.0-beta.25562.4` to `9.0.0-beta.25626.6` (commit `ab5773ac`), carrying the associated `eng/common` template and script updates. It also changes two test areas: the Components E2E browser-log assertion for CSP errors, and the SignalR Redis E2E file (two quarantines plus edits to a `WebSocket` test double used by the stateful-reconnect test).
steps: Version pins are updated consistently: `global.json` msbuild-sdks (Arcade and Helix), six `Dependency` entries in `eng/Version.Details.xml` sharing SHA `ab5773ac`, and four Arcade package properties in `eng/Versions.props`, all at `9.0.0-beta.25626.6`.

The synced `eng/common` scripts from Arcade change agent behavior: PowerShell download helpers add `-UseBasicParsing`, `LocateVisualStudio` becomes null-safe, the source-build job image moves to `1es-azurelinux-3`, the internal runtime feed moves to `ci.dot.net/internal`, and the source-index template default condition becomes `eq(Build.SourceBranch, 'refs/heads/main')`.

`.azure/pipelines/ci.yml` consumes those templates. Its `enableSourceIndex` variable is already gated to non-PR builds on `refs/heads/main` (line 52), so the new source-index default condition does not change behavior for this repo or the release/9.0 branch.

The Components E2E test `EmbeddingServerAppInsideIframe_WithCompressionEnabled_Fails` asserts on the first severe browser log, matching either of two browser CSP message formats (`Refused to frame ...` and `Framing ...`) via generated regexes.

In the SignalR Redis tests, `WebSocketWrapper` sits between the SignalR client's `WebSocketsTransport` and a real `ClientWebSocket`, feeding frames from a background receive loop into `_receiveTcs`. Its `ReceiveAsync` override must support the transport's 0-byte poll read followed by a buffered read for the same frame, which is why the position of the `_receiveTcs` reset matters.

findings.title: CSP assertion uses `&&` between mutually exclusive regexes, so the test can never pass
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/WebSocketCompressionTests.cs` lines 107-110, `EmbeddingServerAppInsideIframe_WithCompressionEnabled_Fails` combines the two mutually exclusive CSP-error regexes with `&&`, so the assertion can never pass - a single log entry cannot contain both 'Refused to frame ...' and 'Framing ...'. Change the `&&` to `||` so the test accepts either browser message format, matching the failure message wording ('match one of'). Keep both generated regexes and the descriptive message; this restores the upstream fix from commit 3132e7b1.

findings.title: Resetting `_receiveTcs` before the zero-byte early return drops the frame the buffered read needs
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs`, `WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync` (lines 406-417) now replaces `_receiveTcs` immediately after awaiting the result, before the `buffer.Count == 0` early return. The SignalR client's `WebSocketsTransport.StartReceiving` (lines 441-461 of `src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Http.Connections.Client/src/Internal/WebSocketsTransport.cs`) does a 0-byte read and then a buffered read for the same frame, so the buffered read now waits for a new frame and the polled frame's payload is lost. Move `_receiveTcs = new(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);` back to after the zero-byte `return res.Item1;` block, leaving the rest of the method unchanged.

findings.title: Build tooling hardening in tools.ps1 is correct
findings.body:
The `eng/common/tools.ps1` changes are a genuine improvement, not just churn:

::diff{file="eng/common/tools.ps1" lines="550-574"}

Adding `-UseBasicParsing` to every `Invoke-WebRequest` in the build scripts removes the dependency on the IE engine in Windows PowerShell and avoids "Internet Explorer engine is not available" failures on agents.

The `LocateVisualStudio` rewrite is also correct: `Get-Member -InputObject $null` raises a parameter-binding error that `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` does **not** suppress, so the added `$vsRequirements -and ...` guards are what actually prevent the crash when `global.json` has no `tools.vs`. Previously, a repo that omits `vs` from `global.json` would fail during VS discovery. Worth keeping as-is.

findings.title: Dependency pins are consistent across all three version files
findings.body:
I checked the dependency update for consistency: all six Arcade dependencies moved to `9.0.0-beta.25626.6` with SHA `ab5773ac30dce73227fa1dff6bf1a21eea67cbd0` in ::file{file="eng/Version.Details.xml"}, the four corresponding properties in ::file{file="eng/Versions.props"}, and both `msbuild-sdks` entries in ::file{file="global.json"}. No stale `9.0.0-beta.25562.4` references are left behind for these packages.

The `eng/common` differences carried in this diff come from the intermediate Arcade updates on the branch and are consistent with the dependency flow. The new source-index default condition (`eq(Build.SourceBranch, 'refs/heads/main')`) looks like a behavior change, but ::file{file=".azure/pipelines/ci.yml"} already gates `enableSourceIndex` on a non-PR build of `refs/heads/main` (line 52), so there is no practical impact here.
